title: Existence of boundary germ lifts in depth two
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, $j:U\hookrightarrow L$, and $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] finite on every affine open. Suppose every $N_y$ for $y\notin U$ is finite and has depth at least two [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Assume the restriction unit $N(V)\to (j_*(N|_U))(V)$ is injective on every open $V$. Then for every $y\notin U$ its stalk map $N_y\to (j_*(N|_U))_y$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0E9I, surjectivity argument of Tag 0AV8; Tags 0AVN, 05AM, 00LL and 00LX

proof.text: Choose a Noetherian affine neighbourhood V of y. Its source module M=N(V) is finite. The immersion U intersect V into V is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its direct image is quasi-coherent with section module P. Use the assumed injectivity to regard M as a submodule of P. On U the unit is an isomorphism. At every boundary point P has no associated prime, by 0AVN and Ass contained in WeakAss (05AM).

For every finite submodule P′ of P containing M, associated primes of P′ are among those of P. On U, localization of P′ equals M, since M already localizes to P there. Form Q=P′/M. On U its stalks are zero. At a boundary point where P′ is nonzero its depth is at least one by 00LL, and the depth lemma 00LX together with source depth at least two gives positive depth for a nonzero Q stalk. Cases of zero source or middle module follow directly from the exact sequence. Thus Q has no associated primes and must vanish.

Every element of P lies in a finite submodule P′ containing M, obtained by adjoining that element to a finite generating set for M. The preceding step puts it in M. Thus M to P is surjective. Localizing to y proves the stalk surjectivity. This is only the surjectivity half of 0AV8, with injectivity provided as a hypothesis.
